reason: Deliberate CD19 wrapping site for the ESLint-compatible CD14 plugin protocol, used by ESLint and Oxlint. ESLint and Rule types stay at the callback/registration boundary; configuration consumers receive the owned ClassAuthoringPlugin model. The co-located test is the explicit native-protocol test boundary: its RuleTester import exercises that RuleModule with real JS and TypeScript ASTs, as required by the approved review scope. Why-chain: 1. Native class-syntax enforcement needs the engines' plugin protocol. 2. That protocol supplies AST callbacks and diagnostic reporting. 3. Typing those callbacks requires the external eslint types, including type-only imports. 4. Keeping the translation and registration in this single file confines that dependency instead of spreading vendor types into consumers. 5. Root decision: retain one explicit native-engine boundary for the approved CD14 fragment slice; the diagnostic-port design remains Helen's separate open judgment (PR34 review5530609166).

Structural CD19 location: eslint-instance.ts is the ESLint mechanism runner's single wrapping factory for the eslint package and @typescript-eslint/parser. It constructs the query and governance ESLint instances, runs lintFiles, lintText and calculateConfigForFile, and maps results into the runner's own types (EslintPort, QueryInstance, GovernanceInstance, LintedFile, LintedMessage) and Zod-parsed resolved-config and plugin schemas. Core and pieces receive RepoPath values, runner hit data and Result failures, never ESLint classes or types. create-eslint-runner.ts depends on the EslintPort it exports, and the unit tests fake the injected CreateEslint surface. This is the one place the discipline-core plugin binds the eslint runtime.
